0_00: The cobra-like puff adder sways a few centimetres, tongue flicking out and back, thick body tensing tighter into its S. Dry grass stirs in the wind around it. Camera locked off at ground level.
0_07: The long leg slams down through the top of frame in a blur, dust and shredded grass burst outward from the impact and hang in the air. Violent, instantaneous. Camera locked off.
0_14: The bird stands absolutely still, only its head turning a fraction as it watches the dead snake. Dust drifts and settles. Very slow push in.
0_21: The bird shifts its weight from one leg to the other, crest feathers lifting in the breeze, head turning slowly. Grass sways. Slow push in.
0_28: The blunt foot flexes once, toes spreading and closing on the dry ground, dust shifting between them. Extreme close-up, camera drifts a few centimetres to the right.
0_35: Both feet hold still in frame while the light shifts subtly across them, a slight parallax drift as the camera eases sideways. Locked comparison shot.
0_42: The eagle beats its wings once in flight, the hare hanging limp in its buried talons, feathers ruffling in the airflow. Camera tracks with it.
0_49: The bird walks steadily away from camera through the grass, wings folded, each long leg lifting and placing. Grass parts around it. Camera holds.
0_56: The bird strides slowly across the vast plain, tiny in frame, heat shimmer rippling above the grass. Camera holds wide, almost imperceptible push in.
1_03: The head turns very slowly in profile, dark eye tracking something low on the ground, crest feathers streaming in the wind. Slow push in.
1_10: The scaled leg holds still and flexes once, armoured plates catching the light as the bird shifts weight. Camera drifts slowly upward along the leg.
1_17: The acacia stands still against the brightening pre-dawn sky, thin cloud moving slowly behind it, the first light warming the horizon. Slow push in.
1_24: Looking down on the nest, loose sticks stir in the wind and dry grass moves in the scrape. Camera rises very slowly straight up.
1_31: The two eggs lie motionless, light shifting slowly across their shells, a single dry stem trembling in the breeze. Very slow push in.
1_38: The female lowers herself the last few centimetres onto the eggs, wings folding down, legs settling beneath her, then stillness. Camera holds.
1_45: The male drops onto the nest edge, wings beating once and folding, dust and loose grass lifting around him. Camera holds.
1_52: One bird steps away toward the rim while the other lowers itself onto the eggs, a slow deliberate changeover. Camera holds.
1_59: The silhouetted bird sits motionless on the crown, stars wheeling almost imperceptibly, thin cloud drifting past. Very slow push in.
2_06: Rain hammers down in sheets, water streaming off the bird's back and pouring from the branches, the bird hunched and unmoving. Camera holds.
2_13: The crow shifts on its perch, head cocking sharply from one angle to another, eye fixed on the eggs. Camera holds.
2_20: The female lunges forward with wings thrown wide, the crow beating away out of frame, sticks and dust scattering. Camera holds.
2_27: The egg lies still, the fine crack visible, a single dry stem moving beside it. Extremely slow push in.
2_34: The crack widens a fraction, the egg tooth pushing outward and pausing, tiny shell fragments shifting. Extreme macro, camera holds.
2_41: The broken egg lies open beside the whole one, light shifting slowly across both shells. Slow drift to the right.
2_48: The wet chick pushes weakly out of the shell, head lifting and dropping, wet down trembling with each breath. Extreme macro, camera holds.
2_55: The chick lies on its side, chest rising and falling hard, one splayed leg twitching. Very slow push in.
3_02: The mother's huge bill lowers slowly toward the tiny chick, pauses a moment above it, and touches it gently. Camera holds.
3_09: The oversized chick foot flexes slowly, pale toes curling and spreading. Extreme macro, camera drifts a few centimetres.
3_16: The second chick struggles free of its shell beside the larger dry one, which shifts and settles. Camera holds.
3_23: Both chicks breathe and shift slightly, the size difference stark, the smaller one wobbling. Slow push in.
3_30: The male arrives at the rim, wings folding, the dead snake swinging from his bill as he steps down. Camera holds.
3_37: The mother tears at the snake with sharp pulls of her head, the larger chick stretching up and taking the first strip. Camera holds.
3_44: The smaller chick strains its neck forward, mouth opening, unable to reach past the larger sibling, then sinks back. Camera holds.
3_51: The chick swallows the strip in convulsive gulps, throat bulging and moving down, head tipping back. Slow push in.
3_58: The two chicks sleep in a heap, breathing slowly together, the light dimming toward dusk. Very slow push in.
4_05: The chick pushes up on its legs, wobbles, and collapses forward onto its hocks, wings flinging out. Camera holds.
4_12: The chick drags itself across the nest floor on its bent hocks, wings out for balance, sticks shifting under it. Camera holds.
4_19: The bare calloused hock joints hold still, flexing once as the chick shifts its weight. Extreme close-up, slow drift.
4_26: The adult stands motionless with wings held half-open over the chicks, only the feather edges moving in the hot air. Camera holds.
4_33: The storm wall advances, rain sweeping in from the left, the acacia bending and its leaves thrashing in the wind. Camera holds wide.
4_40: The monitor lizard hauls itself up the trunk, claws gripping and releasing, tail swinging against the bark. Camera tilts slowly up with it.
4_47: The adult drops onto the trunk with both feet, wings wide, the lizard falling backward out of frame. Violent and fast. Camera holds.
4_54: The chicks stay pressed flat and utterly motionless, only their eyes moving. Slow push in.
5_01: One chick sways upright on its hocks in the grey light, trembling; the other stays down, breathing. Camera holds.
5_08: The small chick lies almost motionless, breathing shallowly, one eye half opening and closing. Very slow push in.
5_15: The single chick shifts in the empty scrape, dry grass moving in the wind around the empty space. Slow push in.
5_22: The lone chick turns its head slowly, small in the middle of the wide platform, loose sticks stirring. Camera pulls back very slightly.
5_29: The parent lands and lowers food into one open bill, the chick gulping, then the parent straightens. Camera holds.
5_36: The chick stands and shifts its weight, its long legs visibly out of proportion with its stubby wings. Slow push in.
5_43: The bird holds a side profile, breathing, crest just beginning to show, the odd proportions clear. Slow drift sideways.
5_50: The chick pushes fully upright onto its feet for the first time, trembling, wings held out for balance. Camera holds.
5_57: The young bird takes its first steps, lifting each foot absurdly high before setting it down, sticks shifting. Camera holds.
6_04: The bird overbalances and sits down hard, dust puffing out around it, wings flapping once. Camera holds.
6_11: The adult walks through sheeting rain with the snake swinging from its bill, water streaming off its back. Camera tracks with it.
6_18: The black quill crest feathers stir in the wind as the head turns slightly. Extreme close-up, slow push in.
6_25: The young face turns slowly toward camera, the bare skin around the eye faintly orange, eye blinking once. Slow push in.
6_32: The young bird leans out over the rim, looking down, then draws back a little. Camera holds.
6_39: The parent stands on the grass below looking up, shifting once, not moving toward the tree. Camera holds.
6_46: The young bird beats its wings hard on the spot, feet planted, loose down blowing away around it. Camera holds.
6_53: The young bird brings both feet down hard on the stick, dust jumping, then lifts them and does it again. Camera holds.
7_00: The bird stamps down on bare ground with nothing under it, dust bursting, then straightens. Camera holds.
7_07: The bird seizes the dry vine in its bill and thrashes it hard against the platform, sticks scattering. Camera holds.
7_14: The acacia stands still over the pale grass, heat shimmer rippling, the distant bird walking slowly across the frame. Camera holds wide.
7_21: The feet come down in a stamp, toes spread wide and rigid at the instant of impact, dust bursting. Extreme close-up, camera holds.
7_28: The young bird stands in tall grass for the first time, head turning, the grass swaying high around it. Slow push in.
7_35: The young bird walks beside the adult through grass, matching stride for stride at half the height. Camera tracks with them.
7_42: The bird stamps and misses, the grasshopper springing away into the air. Camera holds.
7_49: The bird stamps and connects, foot flat on the ground, dust puffing. Camera holds.
7_56: The young bird tips its head back and swallows the lizard whole, throat working. Camera holds.
8_03: The adult stands ten metres off, watching, shifting its weight once, not intervening. Camera holds.
8_10: The coiled puff adder lies almost invisible in the bleached grass, breathing, its patterning shifting faintly. Very slow push in.
8_17: The young bird freezes mid-stride with one foot lifted, head angling down, absolutely motionless. Camera holds.
8_24: The puff adder rears into a defensive S, mouth opening wide, fangs coming forward, hissing. Camera holds.
8_31: The bird's face fills the frame, eye locked on the snake, crest flat, a single blink. Slow push in.
8_38: The wings sweep wide as a shield, the body angling away, one long leg beginning to lift. Camera holds.
8_45: The leg drives down in a blur of speed, dust bursting outward, everything smeared with motion. Camera holds.
8_52: The snake writhes on the ground while the bird is already a full pace back, out of range, watching. Camera holds.
8_59: The second strike comes down hard, the snake's head flattening into the dust, dust exploding. Camera holds.
9_06: The snake lies motionless while the bird stands over it perfectly still, watching for any movement. Camera holds.
9_13: The bird lowers its head, closes its bill on the dead snake and lifts it clear of the ground. Camera holds.
9_20: The blunt foot hangs above the dead snake, toes flexing once, claws clearly too short to grip. Extreme close-up, slow push in.
9_27: Frozen instant of impact from ground level: the foot flat against the snake's skull, contact only, dust suspended. Extreme slow motion.
9_34: The bird steps backward off the snake, both feet clear, wings settling against its back. Camera holds.
9_41: The eagle's foot stays closed around its prey while the other foot rests flat and open on bare ground. Slow drift sideways.
9_48: The adult strides away across the plain at golden hour, long legs scissoring, wings folded, dust rising behind. Camera tracks with it.
9_55: The bird walks away small against the enormous savanna, the low sun sinking, tracks stretching behind it. Camera holds wide, very slow push in.
